summary.intent: Plan and execute phase 49 of cipher-box (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation ECIES unwrap consolidation, expanded mid-session to include batch/drag move parity), then run the full PR-QA pipeline (simplify, security review, CodeRabbit CLI) before pushing and creating a PR.
summary.outcome: Planning completed (5 plans, 3 waves, 6 requirements, plan-check passed after one revision round) and all 5 plans executed with wave-based sequential execution; simplify and correctness fix passes applied and committed. Transcript ends before security review, CodeRabbit CLI, and PR creation steps.

repo: share_keys entries are keyed by itemId (file UUID), not parent folder — file keys do NOT need re-registration after a folder move; the download path resolves by itemId only (verified at sdk-core download handler line 524)

File IPNS key for shared-file re-encryption must come from share_keys keyType:'file-ipns', not FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted (owner-wrapped; recipients cannot decrypt it) — mirrors the updateSharedFileHandler pattern

adoptSharedFolderResult must be called only once (for the source result only); calling it for the dest folder corrupts the rendered view because the sharedFolderTree projection filters by shareId only
sdkCore.moveItem throws 'An item with this name already exists in destination' on name collision — no auto-rename logic needed, error propagates through runWrite to p.setError
SharedFolderClient Pick allowlist in shared-folder-projection.ts does not inherit new client methods automatically — must be manually extended whenever new methods are added to CipherBoxClient

Private-vault batch move is a web-layer loop over single-item client.moveItem (useFileBrowserActions → handleBatchMoveConfirm → useFolderMutations.handleMoveItems), not a dedicated SDK batch method — shared side can mirror the same pattern
SDK dist/ is gitignored and rebuilt by CI — no need to commit built files; web tsc checks the built dist not source, so SDK must be rebuilt between waves when new methods are added
Web package has no 'typecheck' npm script — correct command is 'tsc -b' run from the package root
isExternalFileDrag (from useDropUpload) and DragItem (from FileListItem) are existing shared helpers that should be imported in new file-browser components rather than redefined inline
runWrite in useSharedWriteOps originally swallowed errors and returned void — callers cannot distinguish success from failure without changing the return type to boolean

code.finding: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange is fully key-agnostic (takes raw sourceFolderKey/destFolderKey/fileIpnsPrivateKey with no owner vs recipient distinction) — reusable verbatim for the shared-folder move case
sdkCore.moveItem throws on name collision; error propagates through runWrite to p.setError — no auto-rename needed in the shared move implementation

Pick allowlist for SharedFolderClient must have moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree added — was only listing the 7 Phase 48 methods; new methods are silently absent from the client interface without this
enumerateSharedSubtree DFS already tracks parent during traversal — adding parentId to each returned node is a zero-cost change that enables descendant/cycle detection in the dialog layer
runWrite changed to return boolean; batchMoveItemsHandler now calls clearSelection only on success — previously cleared unconditionally because runWrite returned void
Cycle guard implemented using parentId from enumerateSharedSubtree: compute descendant set of folder(s) being moved and disable those nodes in the picker to prevent tree cycles
Replaced inline drag-type predicate and DragItem type definition with imports of isExternalFileDrag (useDropUpload) and DragItem (FileListItem) — eliminates duplicate definitions

workflow: GSD plan-phase sequence: research → VALIDATION.md (Nyquist gate) → pattern-mapper → planner (opus) → plan-checker (sonnet) → iterate until clean; plan-checker caught a missing REQ-3 unit test on first pass requiring one revision round before execution

Sequential wave execution is more reliable than parallel-worktree execution for autonomous/AFK runs — avoids merge-back protocol complexity and concurrent test RAM contention; it is a first-class supported mode in execute-phase.md

After adding new SDK public methods in Wave 1, the SDK dist must be rebuilt before Wave 2 web plans run; new methods appear in client.d.ts (the class file) not index.d.ts (barrel), so consumers see them correctly after rebuild
Simplify pass should defer behavior-changing findings (cycle guard, clearSelection fix) to a separate correctness commit rather than mixing quality and behavior changes in the same pass
CodeRabbit CLI review runs before PR creation; CodeRabbit also auto-posts a GitHub review after PR creation — /resolve-pr-reviews handles the post-creation pass

Disabling commit.gpgsign at the repo level (git config --local commit.gpgsign false) prevents 1Password from wedging during autonomous AFK runs; re-enable with git config --local --unset commit.gpgsign

GSD executor subagents cannot commit when gsd-tools is not on their PATH in non-worktree mode — the orchestrator must stage and commit planning artifacts (revision outputs, VERIFICATION.md, PATTERNS.md) directly after subagents return

friction: Intel API surface regex extractor produced empty output — had to omit it from the planner prompt entirely and rely on RESEARCH.md for all verified symbol refs
Plan-checker flagged 2 blockers + 1 warning on first pass (missing REQ-3 unit test and two RESEARCH.md doc-formatting nits) — required a revision round that added latency before execution could start
SDK dist staleness between waves: new SDK methods exist in client.d.ts not index.d.ts, requiring an investigation step to confirm consumers see them before Wave 2 could proceed safely
Web package has no 'typecheck' npm script — needed a discovery step to find that 'tsc -b' is the correct command
Git commit signing via 1Password would wedge during autonomous execution — required disabling gpgsign locally for the whole session before going AFK

GSD executor subagents could not commit in non-worktree mode because gsd-tools was absent from their PATH — orchestrator had to manually stage and commit several artifacts (PATTERNS.md, plan revisions, VERIFICATION.md)

batchMoveItemsHandler always cleared selection regardless of move success because runWrite swallowed errors — caught by the verifier as a WARNING but required a separate post-simplify correctness commit to resolve
